key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings favor long-term corrosion resistance, while higher humidity reduces their friction coefficient and wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing detonation-spray parameters to limit coating defects may improve protection of Q235 steel, with wear performance also dependent on operating humidity.
method: Detonation-spray Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel under varied spraying parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, coating porosity, and lamellar microstructure.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and sliding wear under different humidity conditions using Si3N4 balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear trends involve Si3N4–water tribochemistry and may not generalize to other counterface materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
